Enquanto isso, outros programas de domingo à noite sentiram o impacto: 'The Amazing Race', da CBS, caiu 25%, e 'Celebrity Apprentice', da NBC, despencou 31%, provavelmente porque o público escolheu os Oscars em vez da realidade — mesmo que isso significasse assistir ao último espetáculo de Donald Trump.

article_content: Fabian Delph has admitted his Aston Villa teammates were shocked when he told them he was signing a new contract with the club. The 25-year-old put pen to paper on a new four-and-a-half-year deal, ending speculation that he would leave on a free transfer this summer. Liverpool and Tottenham were believed to be tracking his situation, as his previous contract was due to expire at the end of the season. VIDEO: Scroll down for Fabian Delph: Delighted to sign a new contract with Aston Villa. Delph poses with his new shirt after signing the extension at Villa Park. The 25-year-old admits his teammates were surprised he chose to stay. Delph regards his teammates as 'family' and says his decision reflects his dedication. His performances this season earned him a first call-up to the England national team from manager Roy Hodgson. Aston Villa chief executive Tom Fox said several clubs had expressed interest in Delph, who could have been sold for a reduced fee in January. Delph conceded: 'The lads are absolutely delighted. As soon as I told some of them, they looked at me in shock at first. They see a lot in me — how I want to approach my career, how dedicated I am, and how I want to push forward. They're thrilled to keep someone like me here. I see them as family, as brothers — I'd run through a brick wall for them. They're not just teammates.' Villa CEO Tom Fox (right) acknowledged that many clubs were eager to sign Delph. The hard-working midfielder praised his relationship with manager Paul Lambert (center). Delph also paid tribute to Lambert, saying he didn't feel the need to consult Roy Hodgson about how staying at Villa might affect his England chances. 'I got into the England squad playing for this great club. Hopefully, I can keep my spot,' he said. 'I spoke to my family and to Tom. I didn’t feel I needed to speak to Roy about it. It was about not rushing things.' Delph had been linked with Liverpool and Tottenham during the January transfer window. On Lambert, he added: 'I've had a great relationship with the manager since I arrived. When he came in, I was only training twice a week — I wasn't reaching my full potential. He's got me training every day. I spend up to 40 minutes in his office discussing how I can improve my game and hurt the opposition more. I'm really confident about the future here.' Fox added: 'There were a lot of interested clubs. We’ve got a top young player here. The top five clubs are in a much better financial position.'

article_content: Greggs, the beloved UK bakery chain known for sausage rolls and iced buns, has unveiled its answer to New York’s viral cronut: the Greggsnut. After two months of testing, the hybrid pastry—layered dough shaped like a doughnut, fried, glazed, and filled with either summer berry cream or caramel-pecan—is hitting select London stores for just £1, from September 6 through October 1. The original cronut, created by chef Dominique Ansel in 2013, became a sensation overnight. People camped out overnight, fights broke out over limited stock, and supermodel Heidi Klum reportedly chartered a private jet just to bring a box home. Ansel’s version, made with delicate croissant dough, rose sugar, and Tahitian vanilla cream, sold for $5 and was capped at one per customer—yet scalpers still resold them for up to $100 each. Greggs isn’t trying to copy Ansel’s luxury creation—it’s reimagining it for everyday British tastes. 'We saw how the cronut captured imaginations in New York,' said a spokesperson. 'So we asked ourselves: can we make something equally exciting, but affordable and accessible?' While Ansel’s team spends hours hand-laminating dough in a precise, artisanal way, Greggs’ bakers focused on replicating the experience at scale without sacrificing flavor. The result? A flaky, sweet treat that’s both familiar and novel—perfect for a coffee break, not a red-carpet moment. The company hopes the Greggsnut becomes the next big thing—maybe even catching the eye of Heidi Klum herself. 'We’d love for her to order some from us!' they joked. Whether it lives up to the hype remains to be seen—but for now, Londoners are lining up for a bite of history.

article_content: A massive female great white shark, nicknamed 'Joan of Shark,' has prompted the closure of Middleton Beach near Albany, Western Australia, following multiple sightings in the past month. Estimated at over 16 feet long and weighing approximately 1.6 tonnes, she is the largest great white ever tagged in Australia. Scientists captured rare footage during a two-hour operation to safely flip the shark onto her back—an induced state known as tonic immobility—to implant a sophisticated electronic tag into her abdomen. Once revived, she swiftly swam away. Her recent appearances coincide with the stranding of a dying whale calf onshore, whose distress calls, blood, and scent likely drew her to the area. She was detected nine times in a single day—most recently just before 6 a.m.—by sensors in Ellen Cove, part of Middleton Beach. The Department of Fisheries advises all water users to exercise extreme caution and to use only patrolled beaches. The City of Albany has officially closed Middleton Beach until further notice. The nickname 'Joan of Shark' was coined by local fishermen in homage to Joan of Arc—the 15th-century French warrior saint who led troops to victory in just nine days. Like her namesake, this shark has made a powerful, unforgettable impression. Joan is one of dozens of sharks being tracked by Western Australia’s Shark Monitoring Network, which sends real-time alerts via Twitter. This system was expanded after a series of fatal shark attacks prompted a $4 million investment in safety infrastructure and the creation of a Shark Response Unit in 2012. Current policy permits the lethal removal of great white, tiger, and bull sharks over 10 feet in length caught on baited lines—a program currently under review for a three-year extension.

article_content: Italy’s Euro 2016 qualifier against Croatia at the San Siro was suspended in the 75th minute after Croatian fans repeatedly threw flares and fireworks onto the pitch, filling the stadium with thick smoke. Referee Anthony Taylor ordered both teams off the field as riot police moved in to control the unruly supporters. The match stood at 1-1 at the time of suspension. This was the second flare-related disruption of the evening. The first occurred just minutes after Croatia equalized in the 15th minute, prompting a three-minute pause. Emergency services quickly extinguished the flares, and after a 10-minute break, play resumed — though the match remained tense. Italy had taken an early lead through Antonio Candreva, who fired a low strike into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the box. Croatia responded swiftly when Ivan Perisic capitalized on a rare mistake by veteran goalkeeper Gianluigi Buffon, whose failed catch allowed the ball to slip into the net. Despite losing key midfielder Luka Modrić to injury in the 28th minute, Croatia maintained control of possession and created consistent chances. Croatia’s coach, Niko Kovač, could be seen urging fans to stop the dangerous behavior as smoke billowed behind him. Croatian supporters also displayed a T-shirt bearing the image of Zdravko Mamić, the controversial former head of Dynamo Zagreb, adding political overtones to the unrest. Former Croatia manager Slaven Bilić, commenting on ITV4, called the incident part of a broader pattern: 'It’s a big problem, not only in Croatia but definitely there.' With the final score remaining 1-1, both teams now sit level on 10 points at the top of Group H, one point ahead of Norway. UEFA has confirmed it will launch a formal investigation into the crowd disturbances. The match, already memorable for its intensity, will now be remembered for the unsportsmanlike conduct of a minority of visiting fans.

article_content: Former Business Secretary Lord Mandelson has come to the defense of Tony Blair amid fresh backlash over his stance on Iraq. Mandelson argued that while the 2003 invasion may have been a misstep, it was driven by sincere belief—not deception. He rejected claims that Blair misled the public or lost his judgment, calling such accusations both unfair and unfounded. Blair, who has recently urged renewed Western military involvement in Iraq amid the rise of ISIS, has drawn sharp criticism from across the political spectrum. Critics like former Foreign Secretary Jack Straw insist the 2003 war directly enabled the rise of jihadist groups, while others, including Lord Prescott, compared Blair’s rhetoric to medieval crusades. Meanwhile, Blair maintains that removing Saddam Hussein was necessary and that the region would have descended into similar chaos even if he’d stayed in power. Mandelson, once a key architect of New Labour’s messaging, stood by Blair’s moral clarity, saying the modern threat of radical Islam demands decisive leadership, unlike the predictable dynamics of the Cold War. Yet not all of Blair’s allies agree: Clare Short labeled him a 'complete American neocon' and warned that more bombing would only deepen the crisis.

article_content: CNN) — It’s a timely boost for Barcelona as they prepare for their Spanish title showdown with Atlético Madrid. Lionel Messi, one of the world’s best soccer players, is on the verge of signing a new contract with the club. The Argentine striker has had a relatively lean season by his own impossibly high standards, yet he has still scored 28 goals in 30 La Liga appearances. Barcelona head into Saturday’s decisive title clash against Atlético knowing a win will secure their second consecutive La Liga crown. News that the club’s all-time leading scorer is set to extend his stay at Camp Nou is a major morale boost after weeks of negotiations. A statement on the club’s official website read: 'FC Barcelona has reached an agreement to adjust the terms of the contract binding Leo Messi to the club as a professional first-team player. The revised contract will be signed in the coming days.' Messi joined Barcelona in 2000 at the age of 13 and has since won 21 trophies with the club, including six La Liga titles and three UEFA Champions League titles. The 26-year-old was also named FIFA World Player of the Year four years in a row, from 2009 to 2012, and will be one of the biggest stars at the World Cup in Brazil. The announcement comes just 24 hours before what may be the most important match of the season in Spain. Atlético, who will also face city rivals Real Madrid in the Champions League final next weekend, currently top the table by three points. A Barcelona victory would hand Gerardo Martino’s side the title thanks to their superior head-to-head record. Atlético need only a draw to clinch the league. Just weeks ago, following a disappointing home draw with Getafe, Martino admitted Barcelona’s title hopes were over. But a recent dip in Atlético’s form has given Barça a lifeline. Midfielder Xavi, who is chasing his eighth title with the club, insists his teammates must seize this moment. 'We really believed we had no chance, but maybe we gave up too soon,' he told the club’s website. 'We thought we’d lost the league — and things like that happen in football. Now it’s in our hands. It’s a very important title, and we have to stand together. This is an historic opportunity. It will be a great final match. Atlético are the best in defense; they press high, support each other, and have multiple attacking threats. We’re still hungry, and people should be encouraged. La Liga should be seen for what it is — a fight that goes right to the end. We’re facing a great team, but we’re still driven. This is a fantastic generation, and this is an historic chance for us. article_content: Mitt Romney delivered sharp criticism of President Obama earlier today, accusing him of lacking a coherent strategy to combat ISIS. Appearing on Fox News Sunday, Romney said Obama was 'too busy on the golf course to pick up the phone and meet with world leaders and decide what to do next.' He was referencing the President’s decision to play golf just hours after addressing the nation following the beheading of American journalist James Foley by ISIS. Moderator Chris Wallace then shared results from a July Gallup poll asking Americans how they would have voted in the 2012 election if they knew then what they know now. The poll showed Romney leading Obama 53% to 44%. 'I think they have some buyer’s remorse about President Obama,' Romney said. 'I’m not sure how they feel about me—but that’s kind of irrelevant. The real question is how this president is doing. And frankly, they recognize he hasn’t been engaged.' Romney continued, 'The Pentagon was going through ‘what-if’ scenarios. But the president apparently wasn’t. He hasn’t developed a strategy.' He added, 'I don’t know whether you can’t see reality from a fairway, but the president hasn’t grasped the international reality.' Romney also criticized Obama’s domestic policies, pointing to labor force statistics. 'We’ve got about 92 million people who are out of the labor force—that’s unacceptable,' he said. 'The American people are struggling. These policies, both at home and abroad, are hurting people—and they’re responding accordingly.' Despite his criticisms, Romney emphasized he has no plans to run for president in 2016. 'I’m not running, and I’m not planning on running.'

article_content: These extraordinary photographs reveal the striking similarities between humans and our closest living relatives—bonobos. Sharing 98.7% of our DNA, bonobos display human-like expressions, mannerisms, and behaviors—from turning on faucets for a drink to tenderly cuddling their young. Wildlife photographer Graham McGeorge, 42, spent nearly five years documenting these intimate moments at Jacksonville Zoo in Florida. His images capture the daily lives of bonobos: grooming, playing, napping together in the sun, and learning from adults. The young bonobos behave remarkably like human children—comical, curious, and eager to imitate. Adults, by contrast, appear calm and observant, often watching the juveniles with quiet patience. As McGeorge notes, 'It’s like watching human families unfold.' Though these scenes unfold in a Florida zoo, bonobos’ natural habitat is the Congo Basin in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where they face brutal poaching and habitat destruction. Listed as endangered by the IUCN, their survival remains precarious. McGeorge, originally from Dumfries, Scotland, now lives just 10 miles from the zoo. 'I didn’t set out to study bonobos,' he says. 'But once I started observing them, I couldn’t look away. They’re not chimpanzees—they’re quieter, more empathetic—and they teach us something about ourselves.' Even in captivity, their social bonds, emotional depth, and learning processes mirror those of early human societies. As one image shows, an aging bonobo, whose head hair has thinned with age, sits alone—a poignant reminder of the passage of time, shared across species.

article_content: Former Italy captain and 2006 World Cup hero Fabio Cannavaro has been handed a 10-month jail sentence — not for tax fraud, but for stepping onto his own property after it was seized by authorities. Alongside him, his younger brother Paolo — a current Serie A player for Sassuolo — received six months, and Paolo’s wife Daniela Arenoso got four months. All three have appealed, and their sentences are currently on hold while higher courts review the case. The property in question, a villa near Naples, was taken over by officials last October following a probe into suspected illegal construction. Authorities claimed the Cannavaros had never obtained permits for major renovations to the home, garden, and swimming pool. Though the family was cleared of those specific building code violations, they were found guilty of trespassing: prosecutors say they visited the villa for a swim, despite being legally barred from entering. Cannavaro, who lifted the World Cup trophy in Berlin and later collected the prestigious Ballon d’Or, spent much of his club career at Real Madrid, where he won two league titles. His legacy as one of Italy’s greatest defenders remains untouched — even as his legal troubles unfold.

article_content: Athens (CNN) — Wandering through central Athens’ Syntagma Square, Maria Papanagiotaki and Aristotle Skalizos pause to sit on a sunlit bench as they contemplate their future. The couple, who have been dating for two and a half years, belong to Greece’s post-junta generation, having grown up as the country transitioned into modern democracy. While Greece’s turbulent history receded into memory, its political landscape remained plagued by nepotism and mismanagement. But boom times arrived. Greece joined the euro in 2001, drawing back expatriate investment. It hosted the 2004 Olympic Games, igniting national pride. Yet by 2009 — when the government admitted its deficit was out of control — the financial illusion collapsed. Maria, 34, and Aristotle, 25, found themselves caught in the aftermath. They represent a young professional class that will shape Greece’s future — yet they disagree sharply on whether to stay or leave. Their differing views strain their relationship. A few meters away, a man stumbles to his knees, chasing a rolling begging cup before collapsing on the ground. It’s a disturbing scene — increasingly common since austerity measures took hold. Poverty, suicide, and crime rates have risen alongside unemployment and emigration. Maria dreams of escaping to the UK or the U.S., where she has relatives. 'I have to go,' she says. 'I have to leave.' Aristotle insists on staying. 'I want to fight,' he says. 'I won’t abandon my country.' He adds simply: 'I love my country.' They met at their workplace — a German telecommunications company. 'He saw me there, we became friends, he tried everything to get closer... and after eight months, we were together,' Maria recalls. They moved in together, but their finances have deteriorated. Since April, both have seen their workweeks cut to four days. Their combined monthly income is now €1,160 ($1,415), down from €1,480 ($1,805) two years prior. They pay €300 ($366) in rent and about €65 ($79) weekly on groceries — but face added burdens. Aristotle’s father lost his sculpture business in the recession, so the couple now supports his parents. Neither voted in the June 2012 elections because they couldn’t afford the €15 ($18) or €40 ($48) needed to travel to their home villages. New Democracy, supporting austerity, won the election, despite strong gains by the radical left Syriza party. Alexis Tsipras, Syriza’s 30-something leader, resonated with disaffected youth — capturing 33% of voters aged 18–34, compared to New Democracy’s 20%. This shift is striking, given that Greeks traditionally vote along generational lines. Maria would have followed her parents and voted New Democracy. But the party’s fragile coalition offers her little comfort. More than half of Greeks under 26 are unemployed. Among 15- to 19-year-olds, unemployment hit 56% in 2011, according to Eurostat. Nearly one in four workers under 39 are jobless. Some, like Aristotle’s 19-year-old brother Nick, dream of studying fine arts in the Netherlands — but plan to send earnings home. Soldier Marios-Aristotle Koulouris, 23, wants to study political science abroad, then return to break his generation’s 'consciousness of dependency.' 'We need to rise up and protect our people’s rights,' he says. Others have returned. Christina Psarra, 27, worked at the London School of Economics before coming back to Athens to help drug addicts through Doctors of the World. George Stathopoulos, 33, left a career in investment banking in the UK to return and advocate for reform. 'I chose to feed my heart, not just my mind,' she says. George compares Greece’s financial collapse to being caught 'skinny-dipping' when the tide went out. He believes restructuring — cutting bureaucracy and investing in tourism and shipping — can revive the economy. 'The game isn’t lost,' he says. 'We’re just two goals behind.' For Aristotle, the hardest decision lies ahead: he loves his country — but loves Maria more. 'I will follow her,' he says. 'I will sacrifice.'

article_content: Tiger Woods, the 14-time major champion, has announced an indefinite break from professional golf following a back injury that forced him to withdraw midway through the Farmers Insurance Open in California. His performance at the Waste Management Phoenix Open — where he shot an 11-over-par 82, the worst round of his career — underscored the challenges he faces in regaining his former dominance. On Thursday, Woods made a rare public appearance at the Alpine Ski World Championships in Cortina d’Ampezzo, Italy, to support his girlfriend, Olympic legend Lindsey Vonn. Vonn, a four-time World Champion and one of the most decorated female skiers in history, placed 27th in the first run of the giant slalom. In her second run, she posted the fifth-fastest time globally, demonstrating her resilience after enduring two major knee surgeries and multiple injuries over the past two years. In a statement, Woods said: 'Right now, I need a lot of work on my game, and to still spend time with the people that are important to me. My play, and scores, are not acceptable for tournament golf. Like I've said, I enter a tournament to compete at the highest level, and when I think I'm ready, I'll be back.' He emphasized that his current injury is unrelated to prior surgeries and that he is undergoing daily physical therapy, noting he feels better each day. Though Woods described his hiatus as indefinite, he expressed hope to return for the Honda Classic in Florida on February 26. The couple, who have been dating for two years, have drawn media attention for their relationship, including speculation about a possible marriage — a topic fueled by their joint appearance on the cover of US Weekly in 2010 under the headline 'In love with a sex addict,' following Woods’s public struggles with addiction after the collapse of his first marriage.

Sua atuação no Waste Management Phoenix Open — onde marcou 82, 11 acima do par, a pior rodada de sua carreira — destacou os desafios que enfrenta para recuperar seu antigo domínio. Na quinta-feira, Woods fez uma rara aparição pública nos Campeonatos Mundiais de Esqui Alpino em Cortina d'Ampezzo, Itália, para apoiar sua namorada, a lenda olímpica Lindsey Vonn. Meu desempenho e minhas pontuações não são aceitáveis para o golfe profissional. Como já disse, entro em um torneio para competir no mais alto nível, e quando achar que estou pronto, voltarei.' article_content: On Thursday morning, long-distance swimmer Diana Nyad completed a 48-hour swimming marathon in a 40-yard pool at New York City’s Herald Square, raising over $103,000 for Hurricane Sandy relief efforts. The grueling event, which began on Tuesday, was organized as part of the 'Swim for Relief' fundraiser. Nyad, a native New Yorker, described the physical challenge as tougher than she had anticipated. After emerging from the water just before 9 a.m., she was immediately wrapped in blankets and given intravenous fluids to recover from prolonged exposure to cold water. This swim followed her historic achievement earlier that year — becoming the first person to swim non-stop from Cuba to Florida without a shark cage, covering 110 miles in 53 hours. Though far safer than her open-ocean crossing, the indoor marathon still demanded immense stamina. Nyad noted she was 'constantly chilly' and suggested future events be held in warmer seasons, such as around Labor Day. Support poured in from celebrities including Twilight star Nikki Reed, fitness guru Richard Simmons, actor Tate Donovan, and NBC’s Natalie Morales — all of whom entered the pool to swim alongside her. Nyad emphasized the broader message behind her effort: 'We, the citizens of the world, can’t forget these people — a year ago, the storm ravaged their lives.' Her lead handler, Bonnie Stoll, stood by her side throughout the event, helping manage logistics and recovery. Nyad’s resilience and commitment have made her a symbol of perseverance and compassion.

article_content: By Matt Lawton. For Dominic King’s full match report from Anfield, click here. Despite similarities between Brendan Rodgers and Roberto Martinez—and the closeness of their teams in the Premier League table prior to this clash—the Merseyside derby exposed a stark divide in quality and resources. Liverpool boast one of Europe’s most formidable front lines, assembled through significant investment, while Everton continue to rely on loan signings and budget acquisitions. Rodgers and his players delivered a masterclass at Anfield, demonstrating why they are far better equipped than Everton to challenge for a Champions League spot—and perhaps even the title this season. As Suárez and Sturridge once again dismantled an opposition defense, Martinez was forced to improvise after Romelu Lukaku suffered what appeared to be a serious ankle injury. His only option was Steven Naismith—a move that underscored Everton’s lack of attacking depth, especially given Lukaku’s status as a 20-year-old on loan from Chelsea. Everton’s offensive ineffectiveness cannot be blamed solely on Lukaku’s absence. Even before the injury, they lacked the firepower to threaten Liverpool’s defense. A team without attacking threat inevitably suffers defensively—and that’s precisely what happened. Martinez also faced absences in defense: Sylvain Distin and Seamus Coleman were missing, while Phil Jagielka, Ross Barkley, and Steven Pienaar were clearly not match-fit following recent injuries. Yet this was an uncharacteristically disorganized performance from Everton—a result Martinez will not tolerate, regardless of circumstances. He demands discipline and structure, not chaos. Gareth Barry, another loan signing, had been instrumental for Martinez—but on this night, he was at fault for two of Liverpool’s goals. Worse, his collision with Lukaku led to the Belgian’s stretcher exit. For both managers, this derby echoed their respective departures from Swansea City: triumphant for Rodgers, painful for Martinez. In 2009, Martinez planned to marry in Swansea. His immense popularity there meant local vendors refused payment to help organize the wedding—until he announced his move to Wigan. Suddenly, invoices arrived, and by the time of the ceremony, police were needed to prevent disruption at the church. While those tensions have since faded—Swansea fans likely recognize that both managers helped elevate the club with their progressive styles—the contrast in outcomes on this night was undeniable. Rodgers and Martinez share more than age and sharp dress sense: both favor attacking, fluid football grounded in tactical discipline. Their November meeting at Goodison—a thrilling 3-3 draw—was a truer reflection of their shared philosophy. Here at Anfield, both teams lined up in 4-2-3-1, promising fireworks. And there were stars: Suárez and Barkley, among others. But by the time Suárez raced past Jagielka to score Liverpool’s fourth goal, Martinez stood motionless, arms folded, jaw working furiously on gum—not in rage, but in helpless resignation. It wasn’t as bad as Swansea. No police needed here. But being on the receiving end of such a defeat is no joy for any Everton manager. Rather than celebrate two promising young coaches, the night belonged to two world-class forwards: one English, one Uruguayan—and the rest of Liverpool’s red-clad attackers.

Rodgers e seus jogadores entregaram uma aula em Anfield, demonstrando por que estão muito melhor equipados que o Everton para disputar uma vaga na Liga dos Campeões—e talvez até o título nesta temporada. Enquanto Suárez e Sturridge mais uma vez desmantelaram a defesa adversária, Martinez foi forçado a improvisar após Romelu Lukaku sofrer o que parecia ser uma grave lesão no tornozelo. Martinez também enfrentou ausências na defesa: Sylvain Distin e Seamus Coleman estavam fora, enquanto Phil Jagielka, Ross Barkley e Steven Pienaar claramente não estavam em condição física após recentes lesões. Contudo, esta foi uma atuação incomum e desorganizada do Everton—um resultado que Martinez não aceitará, independentemente das circunstâncias. Ele exige disciplina e estrutura, não caos. Gareth Barry, outro jogador emprestado, havia sido essencial para Martinez—but nesta noite, foi responsável por dois dos gols do Liverpool. Pior ainda, sua colisão com Lukaku levou o belga a ser retirado em maca. Para ambos os técnicos, este clássico ecoou suas respectivas saídas do Swansea City: triunfante para Rodgers, dolorosa para Martinez. Em 2009, Martinez planejava se casar em Swansea. Sua imensa popularidade lá significava que fornecedores locais recusavam pagamento para ajudar a organizar o casamento—até que ele anunciou sua intenção de ir para o Wigan. Embora essas tensões tenham se dissipado—os torcedores do Swansea provavelmente reconhecem que ambos os treinadores ajudaram a elevar o clube com seus estilos progressivos—a diferença nos resultados desta noite foi inegável. Rodgers e Martinez compartilham mais do que idade e estilo elegante: ambos favorecem futebol ofensivo e fluido, baseado em tática disciplinada. Seu encontro em novembro em Goodison—um emocionante 3-3—foi uma reflexão mais fiel de sua filosofia compartilhada. Em Anfield, ambas as equipes alinharam-se em 4-2-3-1, prometendo fogos de artifício. E havia estrelas: Suárez e Barkley, entre outras. Mas quando Suárez ultrapassou Jagielka para marcar o quarto gol do Liverpool, Martinez permaneceu imóvel, braços cruzados, mandíbula mexendo freneticamente no chiclete—não por raiva, mas por resignação impotente. Não foi tão ruim quanto em Swansea. Nenhuma polícia foi necessária aqui. Mas estar no lado perdedor de uma derrota assim não é nada agradável para qualquer técnico do Everton. Em vez de celebrar dois jovens treinadores promissores, a noite pertenceu a dois atacantes de classe mundial: um inglês, um uruguaio—e o resto dos atacantes vestidos de vermelho do Liverpool.

article_content: Pakistan’s caretaker administration has authorized a trial to be held inside Adiala Jail for former Prime Minister Imran Khan and former Foreign Minister Shah Mahmood Qureshi, both of whom are currently detained there. The case stems from accusations that they illegally disclosed classified information related to a confidential diplomatic message exchanged between Pakistani officials and U.S. State Department personnel in March 2022. The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) formally opened the investigation in August and filed charges in late September, citing Sections 5 and 9 of the Official Secrets Act — offenses that could carry sentences ranging from two to 14 years in prison, or even death if proven. The decision to conduct the trial within the prison was driven by security concerns, as approved by the Ministry of Law and endorsed by the federal cabinet. A no-objection certificate for the jail trial was issued on August 29 at the request of the Interior Ministry and presiding Judge Abul Hasanat Zulqarnain. Meanwhile, Khan has challenged the legality of holding the trial behind bars; his initial appeal was dismissed by a single judge of the Islamabad High Court on October 16, which found no evidence of malice in the decision. He has now filed an intra-court appeal, set to be heard on November 14. The government, represented by the Attorney General, will argue in favor of proceeding with the jail trial. Khan, who was removed from office in April 2022 after a parliamentary no-confidence vote, was transferred to Adiala Jail in September after serving time in Attock following his conviction in the Toshakhana case. The leaked cable reportedly detailed talks involving U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Donald Lu and Pakistani Ambassador Asad Majeed Khan. Khan has publicly claimed the contents were used to fuel narratives suggesting U.S. interference in his removal — a claim flatly denied by Washington. Both Khan and Qureshi maintain their innocence. Since leaving office, more than 150 legal cases have been filed against Khan, drawing criticism from some observers who see them as politically motivated.

O caso surge de acusações de que eles divulgaram ilegalmente informações classificadas relacionadas a uma mensagem diplomática confidencial trocada entre autoridades paquistanesas e pessoal do Departamento de Estado dos EUA em março de 2022. A Agência de Investigação Federal (FIA) abriu formalmente a investigação em agosto e apresentou acusações em finais de setembro, citando as Seções 5 e 9 da Lei de Segredos Oficiais — infrações que podem resultar em penas de dois a 14 anos de prisão, ou até morte se comprovadas. A decisão de realizar o julgamento dentro da prisão foi motivada por preocupações de segurança, aprovada pelo Ministério da Justiça e endossada pelo gabinete federal. Ele agora apresentou um recurso intra-corte, que será ouvido em 14 de novembro. O governo, representado pelo Procurador-Geral, argumentará a favor da continuação do julgamento na prisão. Khan, que foi afastado do cargo em abril de 2022 após uma moção de censura parlamentar, foi transferido para a prisão de Adiala em setembro, após cumprir pena em Attock, seguindo sua condenação no caso Toshakhana. article_content: Thirty years after its iconic debut, the beloved sci-fi comedy Back to the Future is making its way to the stage as a musical. The production, set to open in London’s West End in 2015 to mark the film’s 30th anniversary, will bring Marty McFly and Doc Brown’s time-traveling adventure to life with live music, illusions, and skateboarding. The musical is being developed by the film’s original creators — director Robert Zemeckis and writer Bob Gale — alongside director Jamie Lloyd, composer Alan Silvestri, and lyricist-producer Glen Ballard. The creative team aims to honor the spirit of the original while reimagining it for the theater, avoiding a mere replication. The story will follow the 1985 film’s plot: Marty McFly, a California teen portrayed by Michael J. Fox in the original film, accidentally travels back to 1955 and disrupts his parents’ first meeting. The stage version will retain classic tracks like 'The Power of Love' and 'Johnny B. Goode', while introducing new songs composed by Silvestri and Ballard. Innovative theatrical elements will include illusions designed by Paul Kieve, dynamic set and costume designs by Soutra Gilmour, lighting by Jon Clark, and authentic skateboarding choreography guided by Andrew Willis, who designed London’s Hackney Wick Skatepark. The production team has conducted workshops in both Los Angeles and London to develop the musical’s staging and movement. With a strong creative pedigree — including multiple Tony, Grammy, and Oscar winners — the team is confident the show will resonate with longtime fans and new audiences alike. A Broadway run remains a possibility if the West End premiere is successful. As Jamie Lloyd stated, 'We want to capture the fun, heart, and energy of the film — not just recreate it.'

A equipe de produção realizou oficinas tanto em Los Angeles quanto em Londres para desenvolver o encenamento e os movimentos do musical. Com um currículo criativo robusto — incluindo múltiplos vencedores do Tony, Grammy e Oscar — a equipe tem confiança de que o espetáculo ressoará com fãs de longa data e novos públicos. article_content: On a memorable Thursday night at Old Trafford, Manchester United honored Ryan Giggs with a Lifetime Achievement Award in a ceremony brimming with emotion and star power. The club’s greatest icons—from Sir Alex Ferguson to Cristiano Ronaldo, Eric Cantona, and David Beckham—shared personal tributes, celebrating a career spanning 26 extraordinary years. As Giggs, now 40, contemplates his next move—whether to keep playing, join the coaching staff, or take charge elsewhere—the night belonged entirely to his legacy. Ferguson, who coached him for nearly his entire United tenure, declared it 'the most special night at the club in many years,' praising Giggs’s dedication, leadership, and quiet influence on generations of players. Pelé and Michel Platini added their voices, calling him an inspiration. Even former teammates like Mark Hughes and Robbie Savage weighed in with nostalgia and playful jabs—Hughes joking that Giggs’s famous derby goal wasn’t even his touch, while Savage quipped he’d lost his spot in the Class of '92 to the Welshman. David Beckham, ever the showman, teased that Giggs still plays because he ‘had Phil Neville doing the running and me delivering the passes.’ As Giggs stood on stage, visibly moved, he thanked the club not just as a team, but as a family—and acknowledged Ferguson as the single most important figure in his journey. With the new manager’s arrival imminent, Giggs’s future remains uncertain, but on this night, his greatness was unquestioned.

David Beckham, sempre o showman, brincou que Giggs ainda joga porque 'tinha Phil Neville correndo por ele e eu entregando os passes'. Enquanto Giggs estava no palco, visivelmente emocionado, agradeceu ao clube não apenas como uma equipe, mas como uma família — e reconheceu Ferguson como a figura mais importante de sua carreira. Com a chegada do novo técnico iminente, o futuro de Giggs permanece incerto, mas nessa noite, sua grandeza era inegável.

article_content: These colorful cocktails are crafted with exotic, fragrance-inspired ingredients such as mandarin oil, bitter orange, vanilla, and Siberian pine needle extract. Designed to mirror the L'Atelier de Givenchy perfume collection, each drink blends scent and flavor into a sensory experience. Created by mixologist Tiziano Tasso at Cafe Royal’s The Green Bar, the seven limited-edition cocktails are available from February 1 to March 31, priced at £13 each. The Bois Martial features Jamaican rum, pineapple, and sage leaves. Oud Flamboyant combines Japanese whisky and mandarin juice. Chypre Caresse blends gin, jasmine, lemon citrus, and subtle honey notes. Ylang Austral mixes rum, sour apple sherbet, orange Curaçao, and mandarin oils. Neroli Orginel pairs cognac with vanilla, lemon, and bitter orange essential oils. Cuir Blanc uses Siberian pine needle extract to deliver a woody, fresh Martini-style profile. Ambre Tigre is made with rye vodka, Dutch honey whisky, and English amber beer. Each cocktail reflects the key perfume notes of its namesake fragrance, offering a distinct color, aroma, and taste. The collaboration between Hotel Cafe Royal and Parfums Givenchy celebrates the intersection of haute couture, perfumery, and mixology. Commenting on the partnership, General Manager Anthony Lee said: 'We are delighted to have joined forces with Parfums Givenchy to create this exclusive collection of cocktails, celebrating the seven fragrances in L'Atelier de Givenchy. Our talented mixologists have showcased the high level of skill required in cocktail design—mirroring the art of perfume creation—in this exciting brand marriage. I highly recommend visiting The Green Bar to taste one in February or March.' This is not the first time cocktails have been paired with fragrances. In 2023, The Ritz-Carlton Berlin launched the world’s first sensory bar combining cocktails with exclusive perfumes and aromas. Chypre Caresse: Ingredients: 30ml Fifty Pound Gin, 20ml Poli Miele, 20ml Lemon Cordial, 40ml Jasmine Perl Tea, a few drops of Pomegranate Reduction. Method: Stir and strain, garnish with a lemon twist, serve in a coupette glass. Cuir Blanc: Ingredients: 60ml Plymouth Navy Strength Gin, 20ml Cocchi Americano, three drops Siberian pine needle oil. Method: Shake and double-strain, serve in a champagne saucer.

article_content: Early Saturday morning in Draper, Utah, a tragic shooting left one police officer dead and two others critically hurt. Sergeant Derek Johnson was fatally wounded while responding to a 911 call around 6 a.m. on South Fort Street. Witnesses, including local nurse Kris Szelag, reported hearing a gunshot followed by what sounded like a vehicle collision shortly before 5:30 a.m. Szelag rushed outside and found Sgt. Johnson unconscious in his patrol car, where she immediately began CPR until emergency crews arrived. He was airlifted to Intermountain Medical Center but later died from his injuries. Authorities have not identified a suspect or determined the nature of the original emergency call. Aerial images show a crashed vehicle at the scene. In the aftermath, police cordoned off a two-square-mile area, deploying armed officers, SWAT teams, and K-9 units to search homes and outbuildings. Residents were instructed to stay indoors unless escorted by police. One neighbor described seeing officers surround a barn, adding to the intensity of the operation. As of midday, Draper Police Chief Bryan Roberts confirmed no known suspects and emphasized that the investigation remains active. 'This is a very tragic day for our department,' Roberts said, assuring the public that every resource is being used to ensure community safety. In a show of solidarity, the Utah 1033 Foundation announced a $25,000 donation to Sgt. Johnson’s family. A follow-up press briefing is scheduled for 3 p.m. local time.

article_content: Despite deadly protests and allegations of police violence, the Formula 1 Bahrain Grand Prix went ahead as planned, drawing sharp criticism from human rights advocates and local demonstrators. Former F1 boss Bernie Ecclestone shrugged off the unrest, quipping that 'there’s no such thing as bad publicity'—a remark that sparked outrage among those mourning victims like 37-year-old Salah Abbas Habib, whose family says he was beaten to death by security forces. Outside the Sakhir Circuit, masked protesters hurled Molotov cocktails and set tires ablaze, demanding an end to the monarchy’s rule. Inside, however, the spectacle continued uninterrupted: drivers raced, grid girls posed, and Ecclestone posed for photos alongside Crown Prince Sheikh Salman bin Hamad al-Khalifa. The government, having spent over $40 million to stage the event, framed it as a sign of national recovery after last year’s Arab Spring-inspired uprisings. Yet, the reality on the ground told a different story. With streets choked by tear gas and reports of a worsening hunger strike by jailed activist Abdulhadi al-Khawaja, many questioned why international media were barred from covering the political crisis—even as F1’s corporate sponsors, like Reuters’ parent company, remained silent. While F1 officials insisted the race was purely sporting, critics accused the organization of enabling state propaganda by turning a blind eye to repression. Sebastian Vettel, the race winner, dismissed the protests as exaggerated, saying he cared more about tire temperatures than politics. Meanwhile, hackers targeted F1 websites in solidarity with protesters, and empty grandstands underscored the lack of public support. Though the event generated half a billion dollars in revenue, the moral cost—measured in lives lost, voices silenced, and dignity stripped—remains far harder to quantify.

article_content: In a rare public address in Mashhad, Iranian President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad fiercely defended his bond with Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, dismissing rumors of a power struggle as baseless. 'Those who suggest tension between us don’t understand,' Ahmadinejad said. 'Our connection isn't political—it's transcendent, rooted in deep respect and trust, like that of a father and son.' He added that attempts to sow doubt are doomed to fail. These remarks come amid growing friction over Ahmadinejad’s appointment of Esfandyar Rahim Mashaie as first vice president—a move Khamenei publicly opposed, demanding Mashaie’s resignation. Though Mashaie stepped down from the vice presidency, Ahmadinejad promptly named him a top adviser, keeping him close. Mashaie has drawn sharp criticism from Iran’s religious establishment for comments suggesting Iranians are friends with Israelis and for attending a Turkish event where women performed on stage—actions considered deeply inappropriate under Iran’s strict social codes. Meanwhile, nationwide unrest continues following disputed results from the June 12 presidential election, which many believe was manipulated. The death of 26-year-old Neda Agha-Soltan, caught on video after she was shot during a protest, became an international symbol of resistance. Thousands gathered in Tehran on the 40th day after her death, a traditional Shia mourning ritual, sparking violent clashes with police. Opposition figure Mir Hossein Moussavi, barred from visiting Neda’s grave, released a video urging Iranians to reclaim the original values of the 1979 Islamic Revolution, reinforcing his continued influence despite government crackdowns.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture is rolling out new proposals aimed at cracking down on people who illegally trade SNAP benefits — once called food stamps — for cash. These electronic benefit cards, meant to help low-income families buy groceries, are increasingly being sold online through platforms like Craigslist, eBay, and even social media sites such as Twitter and Facebook. While most recipients use their benefits properly, officials say a small number of bad actors are exploiting the system by repeatedly requesting replacement cards, then selling them for cash — a practice known as 'trafficking.'

Under the new plan, states would gain the authority to flag individuals who request an unusually high number of replacement cards and subject them to closer review. However, the rules explicitly require states to make exceptions for elderly people and those with disabilities who might lose their cards frequently through no fault of their own.

Currently, federal regulations prevent states from asking households why they’re requesting multiple replacements, even when patterns suggest fraud. That’s about to change. The USDA argues this gap has allowed traffickers to operate under the radar. Penalties for trafficking remain severe: program disqualification, financial fines, and even criminal charges.

But it’s not just individuals. Retailers are also being held accountable. So far this year, nearly 200 stores have faced penalties, and over 360 have been permanently banned for exchanging SNAP benefits for cash. Last year alone, more than 1,200 stores were permanently removed from the program for trafficking, and another 600+ were punished for selling ineligible items like alcohol or tobacco.

To prevent banned retailers from reopening elsewhere, the USDA is developing new tools to block cross-state re-enrollment. The agency also plans to announce additional penalties soon. Since the 1990s, SNAP has transitioned from paper coupons to swipe-style debit cards — a shift that improved efficiency but also opened new avenues for fraud. Over the past 15 years, the USDA says it has steadily strengthened safeguards — and now, it’s taking the next step.

article_content: In classrooms across the country, students are diving into the U.S. Constitution not just as a historical document, but as a living framework shaping today’s politics. They begin by reading the Preamble aloud, then break it down word by word to uncover the intentions behind America’s founding legal blueprint. Back in 1787, the framers designed a system where power isn’t concentrated in one place — instead, it’s split between a strong central government and individual states. This balance is maintained through three distinct branches: Congress makes laws, the President enforces them, and the courts interpret them. The Constitution gives the federal government clear powers like taxing, declaring war, and managing interstate commerce — but also allows it to act in ways not explicitly written, adapting to new challenges over time. Meanwhile, states and citizens hold onto rights the Constitution doesn’t hand to Washington — things like setting rules around marriage, running public schools, and organizing local defense forces. Fundamental freedoms like free speech, property ownership, and jury trials are protected as rights belonging to individuals. At the heart of it all is the Supreme Court, which has the final say on whether any law matches up with the Constitution. Teachers then guide students to imagine how this 230-year-old system responds to modern crises: How does the Constitution handle debates over gun control? Where does federal power end and state authority begin in immigration policy? To explore this, students form teams representing each branch of government, the states, and the people themselves. Each team researches their assigned role’s constitutional powers, then connects those powers to current headlines. Afterward, mixed groups — each containing one representative from every stakeholder — tackle specific questions like, 'Who gets to decide who can enter the country?' or 'Can the president order military action without Congress?' They build visual maps showing which level of government holds authority, citing exact constitutional clauses. Finally, the class discusses how these ancient rules still guide decisions in our digital, globalized world — proving that the Constitution isn’t just history. It’s happening right now.

Esse equilíbrio é mantido por meio de três ramos distintos: o Congresso cria leis, o presidente as aplica e os tribunais as interpretam. A Constituição concede ao governo federal poderes claros, como cobrar impostos, declarar guerra e regular o comércio interestadual — mas também permite que ele atue de maneiras não explicitamente escritas, adaptando-se a novos desafios ao longo do tempo. Enquanto isso, estados e cidadãos mantêm direitos que a Constituição não entrega a Washington — coisas como estabelecer regras sobre casamento, administrar escolas públicas e organizar forças de defesa locais. Liberdades fundamentais, como liberdade de expressão, propriedade e julgamento por júri, são protegidas como direitos pertencentes aos indivíduos. No centro de tudo está a Suprema Corte, que tem a última palavra sobre se alguma lei está em conformidade com a Constituição. article_content: Former Army captain and City banker Brian Witty, 42, is facing new rape allegations involving three women who were all 19-year-old students at the time of the incidents. The attacks, which occurred between 1989 and 1998 in Liverpool, Hull, and London, were only reported years later — after widespread media coverage of his 2012 conviction for three prior rapes and one sexual assault. Prosecutors say Witty used charm to gain trust, then turned violent, overpowering his victims with physical strength when they resisted. One victim recalled how he left her room with a smug grin, as if the assault were a joke. Another described being pinned down in the dark, too terrified to speak, while a third was assaulted in his Kensington flat after being assured she’d be safe. All three women stayed silent for years, haunted by fear and shame, until they learned Witty had been convicted before. Court testimony reveals a pattern: he tracked down ex-partners, broke into their homes, and used intimidation tactics like parking outside their families’ houses. Despite his military background and polished exterior, prosecutors argue his actions reveal a dangerous mix of arrogance, control, and brutality. Witty has pleaded not guilty. His trial at Kingston Crown Court is ongoing and expected to last several more weeks.

article_content: The emergency room serves as the front door of the healthcare system. For most people, ER visits are rare—but when they happen, they can be both lifesaving and overwhelming. Yet, persistent myths cloud public understanding of what really goes on behind those doors. Let’s clear up five of the most common ones. Myth: The ER isn’t like TV. In reality, shows like 'ER' and 'Scrubs' aren’t far off. While not every shift is dramatic, emergency departments can be intense—and dangerous. A 2007 survey of over 3,000 ER nurses revealed that more than half had been spat on, hit, pushed, scratched, or kicked by patients. Nearly a quarter reported enduring more than 20 such incidents over three years. Still, these same nurses often chase after confused patients who wander off, showing compassion amid chaos. Violence in the ER is real, and reporting mechanisms are inadequate. While substances and mental illness contribute to many incidents, that doesn’t lessen the trauma for staff. When you visit, a little empathy goes a long way. Myth: Patient satisfaction is our top priority. You deserve courtesy—just as you would at any service provider. But the ER isn’t a restaurant. You can’t order a shrimp taco at a burger joint, and you can’t demand antibiotics for a cold or a CT scan for minor knee pain. The ER’s purpose is to identify and treat urgent, life-threatening conditions. Legally, you’re entitled only to a medical screening—not a full diagnosis or personalized wish list. A 2012 JAMA study found that higher patient satisfaction scores correlate with higher costs and even higher mortality. Physicians are ethically bound to do what’s medically right, not what’s most popular. Myth: Obamacare will overcrowd the ER. The truth? Crowding depends on local factors—like access to primary care and scope-of-practice laws for nurse practitioners. Even in one of the nation’s busiest ERs, volumes haven’t changed much since 2012. Most people who come believe they’re having an emergency—even when they’re not. Chest pain from acid reflux can mimic a heart attack. Whether you have insurance or not, if you feel it’s an emergency, you’ll come. Myth: Don’t let them put you in observation. Observation units are actually a smart, efficient option. Found in about one-third of U.S. hospitals, they’re designed for short-term monitoring of conditions like pneumonia, asthma, or chest pain. Patients typically stay 16–24 hours. Studies show better outcomes than traditional admissions—in fewer days, fewer missed diagnoses, lower mortality. And if adopted nationwide, they could save billions. Yes, some seniors have received surprise bills under ‘observation status,’ leading to lawsuits. But a 2013 dismissal and HHS data show 94% of Medicare beneficiaries pay *less* under observation than if admitted as inpatients. Myth: It’s first-come, first-served. Absolutely not. We use triage: the sickest get seen first. If your child is bleeding out or your spouse has collapsed, you’d want them ahead of someone with a mild headache. No appointments are taken here—so patience is essential. The national average ER stay is five hours, during which you might get tests that would otherwise take months. Emergency physicians, though just 5% of doctors, handle 28% of all acute care visits in the U.S., per Dr. Stephen Pitts of Emory. We chose this field because we help anyone, anytime, anywhere. You’re free to leave if you’re unhappy—but we’ll be here, ready to help, whenever you return.

Um estudo de 2012 da JAMA descobriu que pontuações mais altas de satisfação do paciente estão associadas a custos mais altos e até maior mortalidade. Dor no peito causada por azia pode parecer um ataque cardíaco. Seja qual for seu seguro, se você sentir que é uma emergência, virá. Mito: Não deixe o médico colocar você em observação. Unidades de observação são, na verdade, uma opção inteligente e eficiente. Encontradas em cerca de um terço dos hospitais dos EUA, elas são projetadas para monitoramento breve de condições como pneumonia, asma ou dor no peito. Pacientes geralmente permanecem entre 16 e 24 horas. Estudos mostram resultados superiores aos cuidados tradicionais — menos dias, menos diagnósticos perdidos, menor mortalidade. E se adotadas nacionalmente, poderiam economizar bilhões. Sim, alguns idosos receberam contas surpresa por estarem em 'status de observação', levando a processos judiciais. Mas um julgamento de 2013 e dados do HHS mostram que 94% dos beneficiários do Medicare pagam *menos* em observação do que se fossem admitidos como internados. Mito: É primeiro a chegar, primeiro a ser atendido. Absolutamente não. Usamos triagem: os mais graves são atendidos primeiro. Se seu filho estiver sangrando ou sua esposa tiver desmaiado, você quer que eles sejam atendidos antes de alguém com dor de cabeça leve. Nenhum agendamento é feito aqui — então paciência é essencial. A média nacional de permanência no PS é de cinco horas, durante as quais você pode receber exames que normalmente levariam meses. Médicos de emergência, embora representem apenas 5% dos médicos, lidam com 28% de todas as visitas agudas nos EUA, segundo o Dr. Stephen Pitts, da Emory. Escolhemos esta área porque ajudamos qualquer pessoa, a qualquer hora, em qualquer lugar. Você é livre para ir embora se estiver insatisfeito — mas estaremos aqui, prontos para ajudar, sempre que voltar.

article_content: LOS ANGELES, California (CNN) — Pop singer Chris Brown was sentenced Tuesday to five years of probation and more than 1,400 hours of labor-oriented community service for assaulting his then-girlfriend, Rihanna. CNN obtained a probation report after Brown’s sentencing, revealing that the couple had been involved in at least two prior unreported domestic violence incidents before the February attack. Brown, 20, was arrested following a violent altercation in a rented Lamborghini on a Hollywood street on February 8. Police discovered two earlier incidents through their investigation. The first occurred in Europe approximately three months prior, when Rihanna slapped Brown during a verbal dispute; he responded by shoving her into a wall. The second incident took place in January in Barbados, where Brown and Rihanna were driving a Range Rover loaned by a local dealership. After an argument, Brown exited the vehicle and smashed its front windows. At Tuesday’s sentencing, Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Patricia Schnegg emphasized that Brown must perform actual physical labor, not generic community service. The sentencing had been delayed because documents outlining Brown’s proposed service plan in Virginia — where he maintains legal residency — were not submitted in time. Brown’s probation will be supervised by California authorities. He is also required to complete domestic violence counseling. Judge Schnegg issued a restraining order requiring Brown to remain at least 50 yards away from Rihanna, or 10 yards if they encounter each other at industry events. The order remains in effect until 2014. Rihanna’s attorney, Donald Etra, stated that only Rihanna herself may petition the court to modify the order. She did not attend the hearing. According to the probation report, the February incident began after Rihanna discovered a text message from a former romantic partner on Brown’s phone. The argument escalated inside the car, where Brown punched Rihanna multiple times, placed her in a headlock, bit her ear and fingers, and threatened to kill her. Police documented extensive injuries: cuts, bruises, abrasions on her face, arms, chest, neck, legs, and inside her upper lip — many caused by a large ring on Brown’s right hand. Rihanna declined to speak to the probation investigator, so details were sourced from police interviews conducted shortly after the assault. She told officers, 'He beat me up.' Brown issued a public apology last month via video on his website: 'I’m truly, truly sorry I didn’t handle the situation differently or better. What I did was unacceptable — 100 percent. I can only ask and pray that you forgive me.'

article_content: During France’s 2-0 victory over Nigeria in the 2014 World Cup round of 16, Chelsea midfielder John Obi Mikel claimed he was struck in the face by an elbow from Arsenal forward Olivier Giroud. The incident occurred around the 29th minute, and although referee Mark Geiger appeared to see the contact, he chose not to issue a yellow card or any formal punishment — only a verbal caution. Mikel expressed disbelief, stating, 'The ref saw it. If you see something like that, you have to act.' He added that while he believed Giroud’s intent was aggressive, he doesn’t consider him a malicious player, noting that such moments can happen under pressure when everyone is fighting for their country. Nigeria’s frustrations extended beyond Giroud’s challenge. Midfielder Ogenyi Onazi was forced off the pitch on a stretcher in the 59th minute after a heavy tackle from Blaise Matuidi, with teammates and staff fearing a possible ankle fracture. Mikel acknowledged the challenge was physical but called it a '50-50' play, emphasizing that Matuidi wasn’t acting with malice — just poor timing. Giroud, who had a quiet game overall, was substituted at 62 minutes. His replacement, Antoine Griezmann, quickly made an impact, scoring both of France’s late goals. While Giroud escaped immediate discipline, FIFA could still review video evidence and impose sanctions ahead of France’s quarter-final match.

article_content: A senior Afghan commander who has advised the UK Prime Minister has warned that withdrawing British troops from Afghanistan could spark a 'global jihad'. These controversial remarks come as David Cameron hosts a high-profile summit at Chequers to discuss plans for combating the Taliban and other terrorist threats following the planned departure of American and British forces next year. In an exclusive interview with The Mail on Sunday, Colonel Amin Jan of the Afghan National Army (ANA) stated that removing British forces would allow Al-Qaeda and the Taliban to seize power. Col Jan, second from left, was pictured with David Cameron and Chief of Defence Staff General Sir David Richards at Camp Bastion in 2011. He also claimed that ANA troops are not yet capable of defeating insurgents — a statement that is politically awkward for the Prime Minister, given that these forces have been trained by UK mentors for the past three years. Britain’s exit strategy relies on Afghan forces being able to sustain security independently. Col Jan — the second-most-senior Afghan commander in Helmand province — accused Western politicians of making misleading assessments of Afghan troop capabilities to justify accelerating the withdrawal of international forces. Tonight, Mr. Cameron will dine at his country retreat with Pakistan President Asif Zardari and Afghan President Hamid Karzai ahead of in-depth security talks on Monday. The Prime Minister has pledged to withdraw all British troops by next year, ahead of the next general election. Already, troop numbers are being reduced and bases in strategically vital areas are closing. When asked if 2014 was the right time for a handover, Col Jan said: 'No, I would say it is too early, because the situation will not have ended. If the British leave, the jihadists will see it as a good sign. A worldwide jihad will take place. That is my view.' When asked if the ANA could defeat the Taliban without international support, he replied: 'Our leaders might say we are able to do the task, but it will be difficult. We have enough soldiers — we have the quantity — but we need quality. We need more professional and better-trained commanders.' 'Do the British want Afghanistan to return to being a Taliban state? That is the prospect,' he added. As recently as December, Mr. Cameron praised Afghan forces for their readiness, telling British troops at Camp Bastion: 'Frankly, the Afghan army is doing better than we expected — there are more of them than we expected — and that’s why we are able to bring home so many troops.' Col Jan, 55, is deputy commander of a brigade of 4,500 soldiers in Helmand, where fighting against the Taliban has been most intense. He is also respected for his resistance to the Soviet occupation in the 1980s. He believes pressure from the British public is driving the troop withdrawal and warned: 'People in Britain should consider what the future holds for Afghanistan and the world. Think about whether you’d like Afghanistan to revert to being a Taliban state and a haven for terrorism. Think about throwing away the progress made over the past decade.' 'The biggest problem we have is providing security in the country’s most volatile areas,' he said. While many local commanders praised the ANA’s growing effectiveness, Col Jan insisted the Taliban would rebound after international forces depart, aided by regional actors seeking to destabilize Afghanistan. 'Pakistan is at the root of the problem,' he said. 'I know what is happening there because I live on the Afghanistan-Pakistan border. Pakistan is training the Taliban across the border and harboring their commanders. The international community must apply more pressure on Pakistan before it’s too late. We also know Iran is involved.' Col Jan has previously advised British leaders. In 2011, he met Mr. Cameron in Helmand; a photo of their conversation hangs on his office wall at Camp Shorabak, near Camp Bastion, where thousands of recruits undergo basic training. Last month, Col Jan hosted Armed Forces Minister Andrew Robathan at Camp Shorabak. Afterwards, Mr. Robathan said the transition to Afghan security was progressing 'extremely well.' Col Jan has also visited the UK, most recently in December, to participate in joint exercises strengthening ties between British and Afghan officers. A British government spokesperson stated: 'Afghan forces are already responsible for more than 75% of the population. By the end of 2014, Afghanistan will have a well-trained, capable national security force of over 300,000. International support for the Afghan government will not end with troop withdrawal. We commit £2.5 billion annually for security until 2017 and £2.5 billion annually for development to underpin Afghanistan’s future stability. It is vital the process is Afghan-led — this is what the Afghan people want.' Meanwhile, Gurkha troops based at Britain’s bloodiest outpost in Helmand, Patrol Base 4 — once dubbed 'The Heart of Darkness' — have handed control to Afghan police after securing peace there. PB4, established in 2009 as part of 'Operation Panther’s Claw,' saw heavy fighting, including a 2009 Taliban attack that killed two British soldiers and injured 17 others. Major Shane Burton, 33, who commanded PB4, said conditions today are dramatically different from three years ago: 'Back then, we were shot at daily. Mines lined the tracks. Now, the enemy’s capability has greatly diminished. Families are returning. Shops and schools have reopened.' After three tours in Helmand, Major Burton credited the improved capability of Afghan security forces as the key factor in stabilizing the region: 'We’re not holding their hands anymore.'
translated_content: Um comandante afegão sênior que aconselhou o Primeiro-Ministro britânico alertou que retirar as tropas britânicas do Afeganistão pode desencadear uma 'jihad global'. Esses comentários controversos surgem enquanto David Cameron realiza uma cúpula de alto nível em Chequers para discutir planos de combate ao Talibã e outras ameaças terroristas após a saída planejada das forças americanas e britânicas no próximo ano. Em uma entrevista exclusiva com o The Mail on Sunday, o Coronel Amin Jan, do Exército Nacional Afegão (ANA), afirmou que remover as forças britânicas permitiria à Al-Qaeda e ao Talibã assumirem o poder. O coronel Jan, segundo da esquerda, foi fotografado com David Cameron e o chefe do Estado-Maior da Defesa, General Sir David Richards, no Campo Bastion em 2011. Ele também afirmou que as tropas da ANA ainda não são capazes de derrotar os insurgentes — uma declaração que é politicamente incômoda para o Primeiro-Ministro, dado que essas forças foram treinadas por mentores britânicos nos últimos três anos. A estratégia de saída britânica depende da capacidade das forças afegãs de sustentar a segurança de forma independente. Col Jan — o segundo comandante mais sênior na província de Helmand — acusou políticos ocidentais de fazer avaliações enganosas sobre a capacidade das tropas afegãs para justificar a aceleração da retirada das forças internacionais. Hoje à noite, o Sr. Cameron jantará em sua residência de campo com o presidente paquistanês Asif Zardari e o presidente afegão Hamid Karzai antes de conversas aprofundadas sobre segurança na segunda-feira. O Primeiro-Ministro prometeu retirar todas as tropas britânicas até o próximo ano, antes das próximas eleições. Já estão sendo reduzidos os números de tropas e fechadas bases em áreas estrategicamente vitais. Quando perguntado se 2014 era o momento certo para a transferência, Col Jan disse: 'Não, eu diria que é muito cedo, porque a situação não terá terminado. Se os britânicos saírem, os jihadistas verão isso como um bom sinal. Uma jihad mundial ocorrerá. Essa é minha visão.' Quando perguntado se a ANA poderia derrotar o Talibã sem ajuda internacional, ele respondeu: 'Nossos líderes podem dizer que somos capazes de realizar a tarefa, mas será difícil. Temos soldados suficientes — temos a quantidade — mas precisamos de qualidade. Precisamos de comandantes mais profissionais e melhor treinados.' 'Os britânicos querem que o Afeganistão volte a ser um estado talibã? Essa é a perspectiva,' ele acrescentou. Recentemente, em dezembro, o Sr. Cameron elogiou as forças afegãs por sua prontidão, dizendo às tropas britânicas no Campo Bastion: 'Francamente, o exército afegão está indo melhor do que esperávamos — há mais deles do que esperávamos — e é por isso que conseguimos trazer tantas tropas de volta.' Col Jan, 55, é vice-comandante de uma brigada de 4.500 soldados em Helmand, onde os combates contra o Talibã foram mais intensos. Ele também é respeitado por sua resistência à ocupação soviética no século XX. Ele acredita que a pressão do público britânico está impulsionando a retirada de tropas e alertou: 'Pessoas na Grã-Bretanha devem considerar qual é o futuro do Afeganistão e do mundo. Pensem se gostariam que o Afeganistão voltasse a ser um estado talibã e um refúgio para o terrorismo. Pensem em descartar os progressos feitos nos últimos dez anos.' 'O maior problema que temos é fornecer segurança nas áreas mais voláteis do país,' ele disse. Enquanto muitos comandantes locais elogiaram a crescente eficácia da ANA, Col Jan insistiu que o Talibã se recuperaria após a retirada das forças internacionais, auxiliado por atores regionais que buscam desestabilizar o país. 'O Paquistão está na raiz do problema,' ele disse. 'Conheço o que está acontecendo lá porque moro na fronteira entre Afeganistão e Paquistão. O Paquistão está treinando o Talibã do outro lado da fronteira e abrigando seus comandantes. A comunidade internacional precisa aplicar mais pressão sobre o Paquistão antes que seja tarde demais. Sabemos que o Irã também está envolvido.' Col Jan já aconselhou líderes britânicos anteriormente. Em 2011, ele se reuniu com o Sr. Cameron em Helmand; uma foto de sua conversa está pendurada em sua sala de trabalho no Campo Shorabak, perto do Campo Bastion, onde milhares de recrutas passam pelo treinamento básico. No mês passado, Col Jan recebeu o Ministro das Forças Armadas Andrew Robathan no Campo Shorabak. Após a visita, o Sr. Robathan disse que a transição para a segurança afegã estava progredindo 'extremamente bem.' Col Jan também visitou o Reino Unido, mais recentemente em dezembro, para participar de exercícios conjuntos fortalecendo os laços entre oficiais britânicos e afegãos. Um porta-voz do governo britânico declarou: 'As forças afegãs já são responsáveis por mais de 75% da população. Até o fim de 2014, o Afeganistão terá uma força de segurança nacional bem treinada e capaz de mais de 300.000 homens. O apoio internacional ao governo afegão não terminará com a retirada das tropas. Após três turnos no Helmand, o major Burton creditou a melhoria da capacidade das forças de segurança afegãs como o fator-chave para estabilizar a região: 'Nós não estamos mais segurando suas mãos.'

article_content: Lt Gen Rana Pratap Kalita, Commander of India’s Eastern Army, acknowledged that while China had a decades-long head start in building infrastructure along the disputed border, India has since launched an aggressive push to close the gap. Speaking at the Gauhati Press Club, he highlighted massive investments in roads, communication networks, and essential services across border regions including Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh. He noted that the rugged, mountainous terrain on India’s side makes construction far more challenging than on China’s relatively flat plateau. To stabilize communities near the Line of Actual Control (LAC), the government is implementing the Vibrant Village Programme — bringing schools, clinics, and electricity to remote hamlets to discourage migration to lowland areas. Kalita emphasized that although the LAC remains undemarcated on the ground, resulting in differing interpretations and occasional accidental crossings by locals gathering herbs or hunting, these incidents are routinely managed through established military dialogue channels. He described the current situation as 'normal but with a degree of unpredictability,' underscoring that peace is maintained despite the lack of formal border demarcation.

article_content: Pyongyang, North Korea (CNN) — Under a blazing sun, two hours of tanks, marching bands, and perfectly synchronized goose-steps unfolded in a grand military parade commemorating the 60th anniversary of the end of the Korean War — a milestone North Korea calls 'Victory Day.' Thunderous applause and chants of 'Mansei!' — meaning 'Long live!' — greeted the arrival of leader Kim Jong Un, flanked by Chinese Vice President Li Yuanchao. Citizens, men and women alike, raised their hands in applause; when Kim waved, thousands mirrored the gesture. Peace, an army officer noted, is precious to North Korea — a sentiment drawn from Vice Marshal Choe Ryong Hae’s speech, which notably avoided mentioning the United States or South Korea, both officially designated as enemies. This marked a shift from earlier rhetoric that included threats of nuclear action. Tensions have eased recently, with Pyongyang indicating willingness to resume joint efforts with the US to recover the remains of approximately 8,000 American service members still unaccounted for since the war. The parade blended history and modernity: dozens of aging Korean War veterans, many in their 80s or 90s, rode slowly through Kim Il Sung Square in decorated trucks, smiling and waving in uniform. Soldiers marched in flawless formation, carrying weapons from the 1950–1953 conflict — a testament to months of rigorous weekly rehearsals. Though no hostile words were spoken, visuals spoke loudly: every tank bore the inscription, 'Let us annihilate U.S. aggressors, blood enemy of the Korean people.' One float depicted a crumpled American flag beneath a Korean tank. Helicopters flew low over the square, emblazoned with messages: 'We will defend Kim Jong Un to the death.' Fighter jets roared overhead, drawing gasps from the crowd. Bronze statues of Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il, alongside giant portraits, were paraded through the capital. The most globally watched segment was the missile display. An officer identified one missile as capable of reaching Hawaii — a claim made during the parade but not independently verified. Saturday, a national holiday, saw tens of thousands of citizens flooding the streets, waving plastic flowers and cheering as they passed Kim Jong Un’s viewing balcony. The parade capped a weekend of events including the opening of a Korean War cemetery and the Arirang mass games. For North Koreans, the occasion was deeply emotional — a carefully choreographed celebration of resilience, loyalty, and military might.

article_content: In a recent study featured on Anderson Cooper 360°, middle schoolers shared candid experiences about how their parents react to interracial dating. Luke, a white seventh grader, worries his parents wouldn’t approve if he dated a Black girl, fearing it would mean becoming tied to a family he doesn’t know. Meanwhile, Jimmy, a Black seventh grader, noticed his parents seemed unsettled by his pattern of dating white girls—even though they never told him to date someone Black, they kept asking why he didn’t choose partners from his own background. Their stories reveal something deeper: it’s not race that separates teens from their parents, but generational perspectives on love and belonging. Child psychologist Dr. Melanie Killen, who advised on the study, says many parents—both white and Black—worry intensely about their children marrying someone of another race. While younger kids hear messages like ‘be friends with everyone,’ by adolescence, those messages shift subtly toward ‘stick with people like us.’ Parents aren’t necessarily racist, Killen explains, but they’re anxious about cultural differences, unfamiliar traditions, and how society might treat their child’s relationship. The numbers tell a different story: according to Pew Research, nearly 1 in 6 new marriages in the U.S. today are interracial—up from just 3.2% in 1980. Still, fear lingers. Luke’s dad, Gary, admits he and his wife once worried their daughter’s relationship with a Black classmate might overlook cultural nuances—not because they disliked the boy, but because they wanted her to think deeply about what such a union might mean long-term. Similarly, Jimmy’s dad confessed he wondered if his son’s preference for white girlfriends meant he felt disconnected from his own heritage. Chantay, another participant, pointed out a painful double standard in her family: if she dated a white guy, no one blinked—but if her brother brought home a white girlfriend, the room went quiet. Her mom, Christal, believes this reflects unspoken questions in the Black community: ‘Do our sons think we’re not good enough?’ She recalls hearing her daughter say things like, ‘Do you like straight hair better?’—a reminder that beauty standards and history still shape modern relationships. For many parents, hearing their children speak openly was eye-opening. They realized their silence—or cautious questions—were being interpreted as disapproval. Dr. Killen warns that even well-meaning parental hesitation can teach kids to see racial difference as something to avoid, not understand. And those lessons, she says, can echo for a lifetime.
